    Pearl (PRL): the multiply is real, the bid is not

    Updated deep dive on Pearl, the matrix-multiplication proof-of-work chain: first-principles unit economics, on-chain holders and pools, emissions, liquidity, and scenarios. Research only.

    Research only. Not financial advice. All times are ET (UTC-4). Labeling rule for this note: every hashrate, supply and market cap figure is marked unconfirmed. Each still carries its source, but none of them has been independently confirmed. Hashrate is an explorer estimate derived from difficulty. Supply comes from an explorer and an aggregator, cross-checked against the emission formula. Market cap is an aggregator figure on thin venues. Charts: market and peer charts use CoinGecko only. On-chain charts use pearlchain.live. Explainer diagrams are simplified schematics. Each caption names its source and fetch time (ET). The price line, hashrate, pool window and unit economics below are the 17:26 to 17:29 ET publish pull. Drawings that still show the 15:22 ET snapshot say so in the caption.

Market cap $348.9M (CoinGecko, unconfirmed). Fully diluted value about $2.19B (CoinGecko, unconfirmed). Circulating supply field 334,582,401. Rank 137.

    The call in one paragraph

    Pearl is still the most serious proof-of-useful-work design we have reviewed, and the team is unusually credible. The token is a different question. Spot is $1.042, down about 6% from the Oct 2 note's $1.11 print, with volume about 44% of that earlier tape. On-chain usage is holding up better than price. Fees since launch are about 7,214 PRL (about $7,500). Issuance at the 194 second target is about $1.06M a day, 50% of the same-timestamp volume. FP8 / Pearl-GEMM is an open pull request, not consensus. Our research view at about $1.042 is Bearish, medium conviction. The book is thin, and a few thousand dollars is the offer, so squeeze risk sits on that book.

    What Pearl is

    Pearl is a proof-of-work Layer 1 derived from Bitcoin. Mainnet launched 2026-04-27. It replaces SHA-256 with noised matrix multiplication, so GPU work that serves AI inference can mine PRL at the same time. Pearl calls this "duplex compute". The core construction is in arXiv 2504.09971. Max supply is 2.1B PRL, with a smooth emission curve that puts half the supply out by block 650,226. The explorer reports a 194 second target and a current block reward of 2,282.42 PRL (pearlchain.live stats, 17:29 ET, height 123,245).

    • Team: Omri Weinstein, Ilan Komargodski, Idan Sugerman. Rafael Pass is research scientist and advisor (economics paper arXiv 2606.06700). Fair-launch claims (no premine, no VC allocation) appear in secondary writeups; we did not audit genesis.
    • Code: GitHub pearl-research-labs/pearl, created 2026-04-19, active on Oct 4 (335 stars, 81 forks, 92 open issues, fetched 15:27 ET; not re-counted at publish). The explorer tip still reports pearld 1.4.8. That is not the current release. GitHub release v1.4.11 shipped 2026-09-29 15:49 ET. FP8 pull request #311 was still open at 17:29 ET (updated 2026-10-04 07:29 ET), not merged, mergeable_state unstable, 31 commits, 42 review comments, 557 files. Head cb102159.
    • Partner: Together AI's May 15 blog announced an "exclusive partnership" and said the Gemma-4-31B-it-Pearl endpoint "is discounted by over 25%, offset by the future value of crypto emissions" (page saved 15:27 ET). The same-day model page says the model is not on Together's Serverless API. Terms of the offset are not published.
    • Pearl's own inference product at pearlresearch.ai is priced in USD, not PRL. No token sink has shipped. A burn, PRL-priced inference, and FP4 in the first quarter of 2027 were floated at a Discord AMA. The 15 September date is in TechFinancials' Oct 1 piece. The Sep 30 piece says last week and Tuesday's session. Both say the notes are second-hand until Pearl releases a transcript. It is not a shipped mechanism.

    First principles: what the scarce unit pays

    The scarce unit is a winning noised matrix multiply, paid in new PRL. Fees are not the metric.

    • At the 194 second target: about 445 blocks a day and 1,016,502 PRL a day, about $1,059,195 at $1.042. Explorer hashrate 53.57 EH/s (difficulty-derived, unconfirmed), so about $19,772 per EH/s per day. All-time fees 7,214 PRL, about $7,517 (0.002% of formula supply). [pearlchain.live stats 17:29 ET; CoinGecko 17:26 ET]
    • Whitepaper (September 2026): each tile of the product "doubles as a lottery ticket for block production." That describes the FP8 spec. Mainnet has not merged PR 311. Weinstein (Sep 25) is quoted as saying the live protocol "is INT-8 only, and adds 10-15% overhead," with Pearl-GEMM "expected to launch within weeks," and spam mining "will always" be allowed. That post was login-walled on this check. The quote is unverified. Do not treat 10-15% as a measured overhead.
    • Unit economics, one GPU-hour that could mine or be rented (ASSUMPTION scale from Basu's June 24 EH/s / 320,000 GPU / 112 MW census to 53.57 EH/s, about 714,000 GPUs and 250 MW): new PRL about 6 cents per GPU-hour; May 31 vast.ai RTX 3090 median rental $0.34 (stale); protocol fee about $0.000003 per GPU-hour. Power cash cost per PRL about $0.14 to $0.85 (base $0.35 at $0.06/kWh, scale 0.8 to 1.2). Rental cost per PRL about $2.16 to $6.88 across that band (median-rate base about $5.73). Issuance is revenue to miners and dilution to holders. It is not protocol revenue. More hashrate makes each coin more expensive to mine. It does not create more coins per day.
    • Reconciliation: Oct 1/2/3 explorer coins 1,065,348 / 897,103 / 994,445 (three-day average 985,632) versus target 1,016,502, gap about -3.0%, inside a 15% band.

    Attention series from X and Google Trends stay off this public note. What we can say from price and usage alone:

    • Price peaked later than the spring usage peak. Daily-series high remains the Sep 28 00:00 UTC point at $1.534 (about 47% above the 17:26 spot). Intraday ATH $1.76 is about 69% above spot.
    • Since the Oct 2 note: spot from about $1.11 to $1.042; CoinGecko 24h volume from about $4.8M to about $2.13M. October active addresses (four-day average about 19k) sit above the September average. Usage is not the thing that broke. The bid did.
    • Claims check (re-fetched Oct 4): Together discount wording verified in the blog; serverless availability denied on the later model page. A "3% to 5% overhead" description of mainnet is not established here. The Weinstein post cited for a 10-15% live overhead was login-walled, so that quote is unverified too. "Mining is paid AI" is not shown in Basu's June software census. Unverified social hashrate and listing-amount claims are not inputs here.

    Analogies and layered TAM

    Useful-work stories have a base rate. Primecoin (CoinGecko, last_updated 2026-09-28) prints about $0.034 versus an ATH of $7.27 on 2013-11-29, down about 99.5%. Bitcoin is only a partial analogy: deep books, 17 years, and work that is not sold as useful. Pearl is 160 days old, two thin venues, about 16% of supply out, and about 92% more supply in a year at the formula.

    Built from units times price (no team TAM figure was on the saved primary pages):

    • Core (in the chain): all-time fee average about $47/day, about $17k/year. Subjective probability that core fees are material in 12 months: about 8%.
    • Adjacent (partner discount): Together discount funded by emissions is not cash to holders. Subjective probability of a second named production partner in 12 months: about 20%.
    • Option (aspirational): if 10% of a scaled fleet ran paid work at the May $0.34 rental proxy, about $213M/year at the 53.57 EH/s scale (ASSUMPTION, unproven). Subjective probability material in 12 months: about 10%. Earliest plausible year looks like 2027 if FP8 merges and demand shows up. That option also assumes the May RTX 3090 proxy can still do the work. The open FP8 branch says it cannot. See catalysts.

    Catalysts and risks

    Catalysts:

    1. FP8 / Pearl-GEMM hardfork. Still described as "within weeks" in the unverified Sep 25 post, with no date. PR 311 is open, not merged. Its pearl-gemm kernels, head cb102159, declare three families only: SM90 (Hopper: H100 and H200), SM100 (datacenter Blackwell: B200), and SM120 (consumer Blackwell: RTX 50). require_arch rejects any other compute-capability major. An RTX 3090 is SM86. It cannot run these kernels. If this branch is what activates, the fork is a hashrate cliff for the consumer cards in the May rental proxy, and a cost-basis reset toward Hopper and Blackwell, not only an upside tail. A secondary account of that AMA (TechFinancials, Oct 1, which dates the session 15 September) says 40-series cards were expected to drop off. We did not hear that session. The kernel list is the checkable part. The branch can still change before a release sets an activation height. That release is the trigger to re-run this call.
    2. A second named duplex partner, or Together's endpoint becoming clearly live on serverless.
    3. A venue with real depth (or a confirmed tier-1 listing). None in the Oct 4 ticker pull.
    4. Attestable proof that a material share of hashrate does paid inference. Fees above 1% of block rewards for 30 days would be an early sign.
    5. A shipped token sink: a burn, or inference priced in PRL. Floated at the Sep 15 AMA in a secondary account (TechFinancials, Oct 1 for the date; Sep 30 for the same notes). Not shipped.

    Risks:

    • Dilution: +26% supply in 3 months and +92% in 12 (unconfirmed supply path).
    • Thin, low-trust venues; issuance already half of reported volume. About $53 moves the BigONE bid.
    • Pool concentration near 50%. Nakamoto coefficient 1 on the explorer's 24h window.
    • Launch-week supply concentration.
    • Rentable, merge-mined hashrate, and two consensus incidents already (July MoE disable; August salted noise-seed hardfork).
    • FP8 kernel coverage, if the open branch ships, strands the RTX 3090 proxy. That is sell pressure from miners leaving, not only a bull catalyst.
    • Ticker collisions, including on derivatives lists labeled PRL.
    • Upgradeable-bridge claim carried, not re-verified.

    What has to be true (and what would change the view)

    Starting from $1.042 and $348.9M. At a 25x fee multiple (ASSUMPTION, range 15x to 40x), the cap implies about $38k/day of fees. Today's all-time average is about $47/day. Gap about 810x.

    Bullish falsifiers:

    • FP8 live on mainnet (a release sets an activation height, then the tip moves) with measured end-to-end overhead of 3% or less, and within about 60 days attestable data showing over 30% of hashrate doing paid inference.
    • Fees above 1% of block rewards over 30 days.
    • A venue with cost-to-move-up above about $250k, or a confirmed tier-1 ticker.
    • A burn, or inference priced in PRL, announced as a shipped mechanism rather than an AMA comment.

    Bearish confirmations:

    • FP8 still open on 2026-12-31.
    • A single payee above 60% over 1,000 blocks.
    • Top-10 balances down 20% in a week on labeled exchange-bound flow (we cannot label that flow today).
    • The FP8 activation, if it comes, covers only Hopper and Blackwell and the RTX 3090 proxy hashrate leaves.

    Scenarios (research only, subjective weights)

    Weights are subjective. Each case models drivers only: FP8 activation, supply growth, fees, and active addresses. No price path.

    These cases use supply of about 422.4M PRL at 3 months (+26%) and about 641.1M at 12 months (+92%), unconfirmed.

    • 3 months, bear (45%): FP8 stays an open pull request. Supply grows about 26%. Fees stay near the all-time average of about $47 a day. Active addresses do not show attestable paid inference.
    • 3 months, base (40%): FP8 is announced but no release sets an activation height. Supply grows about 26%. Fees stay far below issuance. October active addresses (about 19k) hold. They do not confirm paid use.
    • 3 months, bull (15%): A release sets an FP8 activation height and the tip passes it. Supply still grows about 26%. Fees move toward 1% of block rewards. Within about 60 days, attestable data shows over 30% of hashrate doing paid inference.
    • 12 months, bear (50%): FP8 is still open on 2026-12-31. Supply is up about 92%. Fees stay near zero. Active addresses fade from the October print.
    • 12 months, base (35%): FP8 is live with some duplex use. Supply is up about 92%. Fees are visible and still a small share of issuance. Active addresses hold near the October average.
    • 12 months, bull (15%): FP8 is the mining mode the tip is running. Supply is up about 92%. Fees are above 1% of block rewards over 30 days. Active addresses and non-coinbase use confirm paid inference, not only pool payouts.

    Data we could not get

    • Exchange, team and pool wallet labels.
    • A fee time series.
    • Coin-age and dormancy distribution (needs a node and indexer).
    • Current GPU census and power contracts (June Basu paper is the named proxy).
    • Together endpoint volume and discount accounting.
    • Confirmed HIP-3 market row (saved guide page had no Pearl entry).
    • Social attention series (kept internal; not published here).
    • The Weinstein Sep 25 post text. The page was login-walled. The overhead quote is unverified.
    • Pearl-specific perpetual open interest and funding on an allowed venue. The derivatives rows we could read were either a ticker collision or on a venue this note does not use.
    • An FP8 activation height. None is set. A release that sets one is the trigger to re-run this call.
    • A Pearl transcript of the Sep 15 AMA. The sink and FP4 timing above are secondary.
